# Revelation 16: research notes for a verse-by-verse commentary

**About the sources.** Some pages were fetched in full: Enduring Word (David Guzik), Precept Austin and Sam Storms. Those points have a URL but no citation tag. Points from search results have both. I didn't find anything on Revelation 16 from LCMS/1517 (Lutheran), OCA (Orthodox), bibleodyssey.org, netbible notes, or prosperity, word-of-faith or hyper-grace teachers, so those are left out.

**The main split among Protestants:** On this chapter, teachers divide by how they read prophecy more than by denomination. There are three main readings:
- **Futurist:** the bowls are literal events still to come, just before Christ returns.
- **Historicist:** the bowls are events in church history, often tied to the papacy.
- **Symbolic/amillennial:** the bowls describe patterns that recur between Christ's first and second comings.

The same denomination can sit in more than one camp. For example, Gill (Baptist, historicist) and MacArthur (Baptist, futurist) disagree.

---

**v. 1**
- **Traditional (futurist):** Nobody could enter the temple (15:8), so Guzik says the voice must be God Himself. He calls the bowls the "third woe" of 11:14 and says they are partly meant to bring people to repentance as well as to punish. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-16/
- **Precept Austin disagrees on that last point.** Whereas the trumpet judgments were partial and intended to produce repentance, the bowl judgments are completely punitive, the earth dwellers having passed the point of possible return. It insists on a literal reading. https://www.preceptaustin.org/revelation-16-commentary
- **Constable:** The fact that God told all seven angels to pour out their bowls seems to indicate that these judgments will follow each other in rapid succession. https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/dcc/revelation-16.html
- **Baptist (MacArthur):** the chapter really happens immediately prior to the return of Jesus Christ, and is followed by the Millennial Kingdom. https://www.gty.org/sermons/66-56/the-seven-bowl-judgments-part-1
- **Methodist (Wesley):** The trumpets gradually, and in a long tract of time, overthrow the kingdom of the world: the phials destroy chiefly the beast and his followers, with a swift and impetuous force. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/wes/revelation/16.htm
- **Amillennial (Storms):** The seals, trumpets and bowls run side by side and describe things that happen throughout history between Christ's two comings. Only the sixth and seventh bowls clearly reach the Second Coming. https://www.samstorms.org/all-articles/post/armageddon-the-war-to-end-all-wars---revelation-161-21
- **Catholic:** A catholic.com overview describes the bowls as the seven bowls of God's wrath against Rome (15- 16). https://www.catholic.com/magazine/print-edition/apocalypse

**v. 2**
- **Traditional:** The sores echo the boils of Egypt (Exod 9). Guzik says those who took the beast's mark are now marked by God. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-16/
- **Precept Austin** studies the Greek words and suggests painful, itching ulcers that won't heal, like Job's. https://www.preceptaustin.org/revelation-16-commentary
- **Wesley:** the plague falls on the men who had the mark of the wild beast - All of them, and them only. He adds that all those plagues seem to be described in proper, not figurative, words. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/wes/revelation/16.htm
- **Reformed (Ligonier):** those who suffer are those who serve the world, the flesh, and the devil. https://learn.ligonier.org/devotionals/assembling-the-nations-for-battle
- **Storms** thinks the sores are "probably both" physical and psychological. They may stand for all infectious disease in history, and he gives the Black Death as an example. https://www.samstorms.org/all-articles/post/armageddon-the-war-to-end-all-wars---revelation-161-21

**v. 3**
- **Traditional:** The second trumpet hit a third of the sea; this bowl hits all of it. "As of a dead man" means it looks and smells like a corpse's blood. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-16/
- **Wesley:** Thick, congealed, and putrid. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/wes/revelation/16.htm
- **Historicist (Matthew Henry):** The sea turned to blood shows that a false religion poisons the souls of men. https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/mhc/Rev/Rev_016.cfm
- **Storms** says the bowl likely points to the many ways the seas have been polluted. https://www.samstorms.org/all-articles/post/armageddon-the-war-to-end-all-wars---revelation-161-21

**v. 4**
- **Guzik:** When these judgments come, the time must be very short until the return of Jesus. With ecological disaster such as this, the human race cannot survive long. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-16/
- **Precept Austin** argues the bowls are not a re-run of the trumpets: they differ in how much is hit (all, not a third) and in kind (blood, not wormwood). https://www.preceptaustin.org/revelation-16-commentary

**vv. 5–6**
- **Traditional:** It is fitting that people who shed the saints' blood are given blood to drink. They refused the Living Water. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-16/
- **Wesley** reads the title in v. 5 as "The Gracious one." In a time of judgment God is praised for his mercy. On v. 6, he notes that men do not drink out of the sea, but out of fountains and rivers. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/wes/revelation/16.htm
- **Storms** asks whether the "angel of the waters" hints that particular angels look after parts of creation, and answers "possibly." He reads "they deserve it" as referring to the persecutors, not the saints. https://www.samstorms.org/all-articles/post/armageddon-the-war-to-end-all-wars---revelation-161-21

**v. 7**
- **Guzik:** The speaker is either an angel at the altar or the altar itself, speaking for the martyrs (6:9) and the prayers of the saints (8:3–5). He also offers a devotional reading: the altar as the cross. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-16/
- **Wesley:** the altar agrees with the angel and says of God's judgments in general what he had said of one particular judgment. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/wes/revelation/16.htm
- **Ligonier:** when the bowls are poured out, heaven rejoices and praises the Lord. https://learn.ligonier.org/devotionals/assembling-the-nations-for-battle

**vv. 8–9**
- **Guzik:** Judgment alone does not change the sinful heart. "Those who are not won by grace will never be won." https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-16/
- **Wesley:** They could not but acknowledge the hand of God, yet did they harden themselves against him. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/wes/revelation/16.htm
- **Ligonier** compares this to Pharaoh's hardness of heart. https://learn.ligonier.org/devotionals/assembling-the-nations-for-battle
- **Historicist (Henry):** Some take the "sun" to be some eminent prince of the popish communion. https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/mhc/Rev/Rev_016.cfm
- **Storms** links this bowl to 7:16 and suggests it may mean economic hardship, thirst and hunger. https://www.samstorms.org/all-articles/post/armageddon-the-war-to-end-all-wars---revelation-161-21

**vv. 10–11**
- **Traditional:** The darkness may be literal, like Egypt's ninth plague, and it gives a foretaste of hell's "outer darkness." Guzik quotes Spurgeon on fear-driven "carnal repentance" that does not truly change a person. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-16/
- **Wesley:** The fifth bowl hits the beast's throne, the sixth the Mahometans, the seventh chiefly the heathens. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/wes/revelation/16.htm
- **Storms:** The throne stands for the centre of a world system of idolatry, and the darkness is spiritual confusion. He argues that literal darkness alone could not cause pain bad enough to make people gnaw their tongues. https://www.samstorms.org/all-articles/post/armageddon-the-war-to-end-all-wars---revelation-161-21

**v. 12**
- **Futurist:** Guzik suggests eastern armies (he names China, India and Japan) crossing the dried-up river. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-16/
- **Constable** mentions an Oriental invasion of Babylon in the future that will be similar to Cyrus' invasion and the Parthians of John's own day. He prefers Oriental armies gathering for Armageddon. https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/dcc/revelation-16.html
- **Historicist (Henry):** This probably shows the destruction of the Turkish power, and of idolatry, and that a way will be made for the return of the Jews. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/revelation/16-16.htm
- **Amillennial (Storms):** The verse is built on the Euphrates being diverted when Cyrus took Babylon. "Kings from the east" was a standard Old Testament phrase for Israel's invaders. It "does not refer to the armies of Red China." He also mentions, and rejects, La Rondelle's view that these kings are Christ's angelic armies. https://www.samstorms.org/all-articles/post/armageddon-the-war-to-end-all-wars---revelation-161-21

**vv. 13–14**
- **Traditional:** Jews counted frogs unclean, while Egyptians worshipped a frog-goddess. Guzik compares the spirits to the lying spirit sent to Ahab (1 Kings 22) and notes that signs and wonders are tools of deception. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-16/
- **Constable:** The demons go out to the kings of the earth deceiving them to assemble their armies in Palestine for the battle of Armageddon. https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/dcc/revelation-16.html
- **Storms** says the frogs are metaphors, since they "perform signs." Following Beale, they stand for confusion caused by deception. He stresses that the Greek says "*the* war," the well-known final battle. https://www.samstorms.org/all-articles/post/armageddon-the-war-to-end-all-wars---revelation-161-21

**v. 15**
- **Guzik:** The garments stand for the righteousness Christ gives and for practical holiness. Being "naked" means trying to cover yourself, as Adam did. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-16/
- **Pre-tribulation reading (Precept Austin):** Jesus comes for those who are watching in the *Rapture* of the Church prior to this time. https://www.preceptaustin.org/revelation-16-commentary
- **Constable** gives a second view: the warning is for church-age readers, before the Tribulation begins. https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/dcc/revelation-16.html
- **Wesley:** "Naked" means losing the graces which he takes no care to keep. https://www.ccel.org/w/wesley/notes/notes/Revelation.html

**v. 16: the sharpest disagreement**
- **A literal place:**
  - Guzik: it is "best" to take it as the literal region of Megiddo and the Esdraelon valley. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-16/
  - Precept Austin: a real river implies a real place. https://www.preceptaustin.org/revelation-16-commentary
  - Biblehub's study notes call Armageddon the staging ground; Jerusalem is the finish line. https://biblehub.com/revelation/16-16.htm
- **A symbol:**
  - Ellicott: The old battle-ground becomes the symbol of the decisive struggle. It is raised in meaning: it is a type, not a locality. https://biblehub.com/revelation/16-16.htm
  - Pulpit Commentary: the Hebrew name draws attention is called to the symbolical nature of the name. https://biblehub.com/revelation/16-16.htm
  - Reformed (Ligonier): John well knows that Megiddo is not a mountain; he is using language symbolically. https://learn.ligonier.org/devotionals/assembling-the-nations-for-battle
- **Lutheran (Lenski, quoted by Coffman):** "Not a word is said about the Lord God's army." https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/bcc/revelation-16.html
- **Methodist:**
  - Clarke mocks predictions that put the battle at Austerlitz, Moscow or Waterloo. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/revelation/16-16.html
  - Wesley: Armageddon signifies the city or the mountain of Megiddo; to which the valley of Megiddo adjoined. https://www.ccel.org/w/wesley/notes/notes/Revelation.html
- **Amillennial (Storms):** The same battle appears in 16:12–16, 19:17–21 and 20:7–10. Although each has a different focus, they are complementary portrayals of the second coming of Christ. https://www.samstorms.org/enjoying-god-blog/post/armageddon--what-and-when-
- **Possible meanings of the name:** "Mount of assembly" (Torrey, via Bruce, citing Isa 14:13). https://www.preceptaustin.org/revelation-16-commentary

**v. 17**
- **Wesley:** "Air" is the bowl Which encompasses the whole earth. This is the most weighty phial of all. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/wes/revelation/16.htm
- **Guzik:** after this there is finality and no more delay. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-16/
- **Biblehub notes** compare "It is done" with "It is finished" (John 19:30). https://biblehub.com/q/Why_are_the_seven_bowls_important.htm

**v. 18**
- **Wesley:** It was therefore a literal, not figurative, earthquake. https://www.ccel.org/w/wesley/notes/notes/Revelation.html
- **Constable:** the seals, trumpets and bowls all three series of judgments end at the same time. https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/dcc/revelation-16.html

**v. 19: who is "the great city"?**
- **Babylon:** The Pulpit Commentary leaves scarcely any doubt that the "great city" here is Babylon. https://biblehub.com/revelation/16-19.htm
- **Jerusalem:**
  - Wesley: Namely, Jerusalem, here opposed to the heathen cities in general, and in particular to Rome. https://www.ccel.org/w/wesley/notes/notes/Revelation.html
  - The Cambridge Bible suggests a possible link to the three factions inside Jerusalem during Titus's siege. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/revelation/16-19.html
- **Historicist:** Gill takes it as the whole Romish jurisdiction. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/revelation/16-19.htm
- **Symbolic:** Coffman, citing Leon Morris, takes it as urban civilization breaking apart completely. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/revelation/16-19.html

**v. 20**
- **Coffman:** in Scripture, such upheavals are "such things are invariably associated with the final judgment". https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/bcc/revelation-16.html

**v. 21**
- **Precept Austin:** the hailstones would strike at about 180 mph. https://www.preceptaustin.org/revelation-16-commentary
- **Guzik:** even this cannot break the stubbornness of the unrepentant, who blaspheme God in the very moment of their judgment. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-16/
- **Symbolic (Bible Study NT):** these verses are symbolic of the *horror* of Judgment. https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/ice/revelation-16.html
